teaching_card.title: Trends, Interpolation and Extrapolation (Hard)
teaching_card.body: Many questions ask what the data would show between two rows or beyond the last one. The method is always the same: find the direction of the trend, find the two rows that bracket the value you need, and assume the change continues smoothly. Between rows, the answer sits between the two listed values. Beyond the table, continue the last step at the same rate unless the data are clearly leveling off or speeding up.
key_points: Describe the trend from the row-to-row changes, not from one glance.
Interpolation: the answer lies between the values of the bracketing rows.
Extrapolation: continue the pattern of the last rows in the same direction.
Steady, slowing, or accelerating? Compare the sizes of successive changes.
If x doubles, divide the two y values to see what happened to y.
A rate of change is Δy ÷ Δx; to compare two series over the same interval, compare their Δy values.
Two series heading toward each other cross when the faster one catches up; continue both at their last rates.
teaching_card.worked_example: Stretch: 100 g → 4.0 cm, 200 g → 8.0 cm, 300 g → 12.0 cm. At 250 g the stretch is between 8.0 and 12.0, about 10.0 cm. At 400 g, continuing the +4.0 per 100 g step gives 16.0 cm.

screens.title: Name the trend precisely
screens.body: Subtract each value from the next. All positive means increasing; all negative means decreasing. Then look at the sizes of those changes: about equal means a steady (linear) trend, shrinking means the curve is leveling off, growing means it is accelerating. Those distinctions are exactly what the answer choices test.
key_points: Direction comes from the sign of each change.
Pace comes from whether the changes shrink, grow, or stay the same.

screens.title: Reading between the rows
screens.body: To predict a value for an x that was not tested, find the two tested x values on either side of it. The prediction must fall between their y values. Halfway between the x values means roughly halfway between the y values; a quarter of the way means closer to the nearer row.
screens.worked_example: 40 cm → 1.27 s and 60 cm → 1.55 s. At 50 cm: about halfway, so ≈ 1.41 s. 'Between 1.27 and 1.55' is the safe answer form.

screens.title: Reading beyond the table
screens.body: To predict past the last row, use the change between the last two rows and add it again for each additional step. If asked when a target will be reached, count how many of those steps are needed. For a decreasing trend, the next value is lower than the last, never back up among earlier values.
key_points: Next value = last value + last change (per step).
Steps needed = (target − last) ÷ change per step.

screens.title: Doubling and crossing
screens.body: If the question says x doubled, divide the y at 2x by the y at x. A ratio near 2 means y doubled; near 4, quadrupled; near 0.25, fell to a quarter; between 1 and 2, increased but less than doubled. For two series, compare them row by row to find where one first passes the other or where they are closest.
key_points: Ratio y(2x) ÷ y(x) tells the story in one division.
Crossing: compare the two columns row by row.
